items.finding: The 24% attributable fraction cannot be reproduced from its printed inputs (case-based formula: 34.9% from 218/410 and 2.91, outside the printed 17.4 to 30.6; 20.5% for daily skunk use against 16.0%, 14.0 to 20.3; only daily use, 20.1% against 19.3%, comes close).
items.reason: Recomputed: pc x (OR - 1)/OR gives 20.1%, 34.9% and 20.5% from Table 4's own inputs; 24.0% would need an odds ratio of about 1.82 at 53% exposure, or about 150 exposed cases at 2.91; Levin's formula with the controls' prevalence (Table 2) gives 26.5%, not 24.0%. The Methods (p. 234, Statistical analysis, 3rd paragraph) name exactly the inputs of the case-based formula (prevalence of exposure in cases and the odds ratio). The claim already says the 24% cannot be reproduced and that it assumes causality; no change to the statement. The recomputed values stay on the card and in anchor 5, not in the claim's numbers, so they cannot be read as the study's result.
